title: Z3 5.3.1's whole output for 40 SMT-LIB queries through the command line and the Python API under an rlimit: the verdict-line fixtures of the Z3 lane
records: the outputs that the Z3 lane's verdict-line grammar and its fixture are written from: answers, reasons, errors before and after the answer with their exit codes, Z3's refusal of an rlimit above 2^32 - 1, check-sat-assuming through both entries, an assertion after the question, a script's own :rlimit replacing the command line's, a printed word that reads as an answer, an echoed answer before a stray parenthesis, a block comment that hides an echo, a backslash in a quoted symbol, named premises through both entries (with the answer of the parse_smt2_string reading the api entry no longer uses), a nonlinear term under QF_LIA through both entries, premises split by a NUL in a comment, a guard after a bare carriage return in a comment and a CRLF string literal through both entries (with the Path.read_text reading the api entry no longer uses), a DIMACS header, a named assumption, an assumption annotated with the quoted symbol |!|, an assumed Boolean constant tied to the formula through both entries, values and a term printed after the answer and before the model through both entries, and models turned off or printed as text; with the answers Solver.from_string gives to the NUL and DIMACS texts, and the answer under the named assumption read as the api entry reads an assumption, all of which the lane refuses
binary: bin/z3 from the z3-solver 5.3.1.0 wheel (bench/uv.lock), which statespace doctor pins as z3-cli; the api cases load lib/libz3.so from the same wheel (sha256 under configs and values), which doctor pins as z3

budget.cases: every case ran under rlimit=5000000 except cli-rlimit-too-large (4294967296, which Z3 refuses); timeout_s is the capture's wall-clock backstop, 3 s for cli-script-rlimit-overrides

parse_smt2_string_reading.how: in a fresh Python process (python -I), on the library the api cases load: z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000, add(parse_smt2_string(<prefix>)) with <prefix> = the case's text before (check-sat), check()
parse_smt2_string_reading.why: parse_smt2_string returns each named assertion as (=> name formula), and nothing assumes the name

from_string_nul_reading.how: in a fresh Python process (python -I), on the library the api cases load: z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000, from_string(<prefix>) with <prefix> = the case's text before (check-sat), check()
from_string_nul_reading.why: from_string passes the text to Z3 as a C string, which ends at the NUL, so it reads the first premise alone

from_string_dimacs_reading.how: in a fresh Python process (python -I), on the library the api cases load: z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000, from_string(<prefix>) with <prefix> = the case's text before (check-sat), check()
from_string_dimacs_reading.why: from_string reads a text that starts 'p c' as DIMACS, whose clauses 1 and -1 contradict each other

read_text_cr_reading.how: in a fresh Python process (python -I), on the library the api cases load: z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000, from_string(<prefix>) with <prefix> = Path.read_text of a file holding the case's text, then its text before (check-sat), check()
read_text_cr_reading.why: Path.read_text turns the bare carriage return into a line feed, which ends the comment before the guard

parse_smt2_string_assumption_reading.how: in a fresh Python process (python -I), on the library the api cases load: z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000, from_string(<prefix>) with <prefix> = the case's text before (check-sat-assuming, check(*assumptions), each of the question's assumptions read as the api entry reads one, the last formula of parse_smt2_string(<prefix> + (assert <assumption>))
parse_smt2_string_assumption_reading.why: with unsat cores on, parse_smt2_string returns the named assumption as an implication from its name (assumptions_read), which the name's being false satisfies

from_string_produce_models_off_reading.how: in a fresh Python process (python -I), on the library the api cases load: z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000, from_string(<prefix>) with <prefix> = the case's text before (check-sat), check()

unrecorded.reason: the run is 40 commands, each with its own exit code: values.cases.<case>.exit_code, and the -- exit line after each case in verdict_lines and capture.log

notes: Recorded by W1-T29 with scripts/spikes/W1-T29/capture-z3-lines.py, which writes this record, the fixture bench/statespace/check/fixtures/z3-verdict-lines.json, the queries under runs/RUN-z3-verdict-lines/queries/ and the transcript runs/RUN-z3-verdict-lines/capture.log from one execution. Each case ran in a scratch directory holding its query, so argv names the input by file name.

verdict_lines holds, for each case, the transcript's == line naming the case and its command, the lines of Z3's output that the Z3 lane's grammar keeps (the answer, a reason that is not empty, every (error ...) line), or Z3's whole output when it holds none of those, and the transcript's -- line with the exit code. Models are not verdict lines; capture.log and the fixture hold every output verbatim.

One configuration per case, named by the case: its command, its query, the hash of what ran (the z3 binary for a cli case, the native library for an api case), its exit code and its verdict lines. The top level lists every command in the order they ran, so it names no primary configuration.

The expectations in the fixture (verdict lines, verdict, reason) are stated by hand in the capture script from the grammar, not computed by the lane, and the lane's tests read every captured output against them; the drift test in bench/statespace/check/tests/test_z3_lane.py re-executes every case against the pinned engine. statespace run re-executes a cli case with --config <case> where the pinned z3 is on PATH (uv run --project bench --group image); it does not re-execute the top level, whose argv holds several commands, or an api case, whose runner is the CLI's own code.

cli-script-rlimit-overrides: a 3 s wall-clock limit of the capture's own stopped Z3, so its exit code is null; the same query under the command line's rlimit=5000000 without the option stops with unknown (canceled) in cli-unknown-rlimit.

cli-syntax-error-no-answer, cli-stray-paren-after-echo, cli-block-comment-hides-echo, cli-backslash-in-quoted-symbol, cli-nul-in-comment, cli-dimacs-prefix, cli-named-assumption, cli-quoted-annotation-assumption, cli-produce-models-off, cli-model-off and cli-model-v1-text run Z3 directly on scripts that the Z3 lane refuses before they reach Z3 (check_script): they record why it refuses them.

Each case's query is written and read as bytes, and its output decoded as UTF-8 with no line-ending translation, so the carriage returns of cli-cr-in-comment, cli-crlf-string and their api twins reach Z3 as given, and the NUL of cli-nul-in-comment too.

values.<reading>: readings of a case's text through Z3's Python API, each in a fresh Python process (python -I; within one process, the API kept the names earlier texts defined, and a later reading's model defined them too), on the library the api cases load, each the text before the case's question read into z3.Solver() under rlimit=5000000 and checked, under the question's assumptions when the reading lists them (each read as the api entry reads an assumption, and listed as read under assumptions_read), and for the readings that record it, the model after sat as the api entry printed it, model().sexpr() (under model, with the names it defines under model_defines); they are the last == blocks of capture.log and of verdict_lines. parse_smt2_string_reading: sat for api-named-premises (parse_smt2_string returns each named assertion as (=> name formula), and nothing assumes the name); from_string_nul_reading: sat for cli-nul-in-comment (from_string passes the text to Z3 as a C string, which ends at the NUL, so it reads the first premise alone); from_string_dimacs_reading: unsat for cli-dimacs-prefix (from_string reads a text that starts 'p c' as DIMACS, whose clauses 1 and -1 contradict each other); read_text_cr_reading: unsat for cli-cr-in-comment (Path.read_text turns the bare carriage return into a line feed, which ends the comment before the guard); parse_smt2_string_assumption_reading: sat for cli-named-assumption (with unsat cores on, parse_smt2_string returns the named assumption as an implication from its name (assumptions_read), which the name's being false satisfies); from_string_produce_models_off_reading: sat for cli-produce-models-off (the api entry read the script this way and printed its solver's model, model().sexpr(), where the command line prints none); from_string_model_v1_reading: sat for cli-model-v1-text (the api entry read the script this way and printed its solver's model, model().sexpr(), where the command line prints the model as a quoted string). Through the lane, both entries answer unsat to the named premises and sat to the guard after a carriage return, and the NUL and DIMACS texts, the annotated questions and the scripts that turn models off or print them as text never reach Z3.
